segments.title: 第32章 大佬
segments.content:
After dinner, Xu Youyu leaned back comfortably in her chair, rubbed her full belly, and let out a contented sigh.

"So delicious." She couldn't help but sigh. "If you opened a restaurant, it would definitely be packed with customers every day."

"You're welcome." Li Luo picked his teeth with a toothpick, then said, "I can cook every day in the future."

"For real?"

"Of course it's real." Li Luo chuckled. "But there are three things I won't do."

"What three things won't you do?" Ying Chanxi, who was beside them, asked curiously.

"I won't do the grocery shopping."

"I won't do the dishes."

"I won't take out the trash."

Li Luo slowly held up three fingers as he spoke.

"That's easy." Xu Youyu raised an eyebrow and stood up from her chair. "Then I'll do the dishes today."

"I'll help." Ying Chanxi also got up. "You just be in charge of cooking, leave the rest to us."

"OK." Li Luo snapped his fingers in satisfaction. "Junzi, want to go play on the computer with me?"

"No, I can't." Zhao Rongjun shook his head. "I still have some homework I haven't finished. I have to go back tonight to catch up. I have class tomorrow."

"You have it so rough," Li Luo couldn't help but say. "You still have to do homework during the transition from junior high to high school."

"It's not so bad. Ying Chanxi has to do it too."

"Don't you usually finish it during class?" Ying Chanxi said, blinking, as she cleared the bowls and chopsticks from the table. "Unless it's homework assigned by the teacher in the last period, I never leave it to do at home."

Zhao Rongjun was speechless.

Li Luo tut-tutted and patted Zhao Rongjun's shoulder. "Even among top students, there's a gap. Little Jun, you still have a long way to go."

"You have the nerve to say that about him," Ying Chanxi said, rolling her eyes. "Worry about yourself first. The teachers said there'll be a placement test at the start of the semester. Don't just fool around all summer break. Review a little, or your grades will slip."

"Will I get expelled from Fuyi High if my grades slip?" Li Luo's expression turned serious as he asked sternly.

"N-No, you won't..."

"Then it's fine." Li Luo's serious face instantly vanished, and he let out a couple of chuckles. "When it's time to play, you have to play hard. School time is for studying hard."

Ying Chanxi gave him a speechless, sidelong glance. "You have the most twisted logic."

The two girls carried the plates, bowls, and chopsticks from the table into the kitchen and started cleaning up and washing the dishes.

Li Luo saw Zhao Rongjun out. As he passed by the kitchen, he glanced at the two slender figures inside, then returned to his master bedroom, closed the door, and sat down at his desk with a clear conscience to turn on his computer.

Playing basketball with Zhao Rongjun this afternoon had slightly affected his progress on his manuscript buffer.

Li Luo glanced at the current word count of what had been published: a total of 210,000 words.

And the total word count of the entire book in his draft box was already over 400,000 words.

After all, he was a man with a memory palace. Although he wasn't directly transcribing a certain book, he already had experience in writing web novels and a large number of market-tested plot examples from the future to draw from. Li Luo's typing speed was remarkably fast.

At this rate, by the time he enrolled and attended military training, he should be able to write around 500,000 words.

By then, he would have a manuscript buffer of about 250,000 words, which should be more than enough to handle the busy high school life after school started.

With this in mind, Li Luo opened his writing software while logging into his QQ.

Then he saw the message his editor had sent during the day.

Qianzhou: Reignition, are you there? We're going premium next Friday, remember to build up your chapter buffer.

About an hour or two later, a few more messages came through.

Qianzhou: By the way, do you want to add "Sleeping Early Will Make You Taller"? She's another entertainment genre author who debuted around the same time as you, and both of you are under me.

Qianzhou: Her numbers are a little weaker than yours. I was thinking, could you two do a chapter shout-out for each other?

Qianzhou: I've sent her your QQ contact info, so you two can chat privately about it.

Huh?!

Seeing the editor's message, Li Luo was suddenly jolted. He immediately checked his friend requests page and found that it was indeed Xu Youyu who had sent him a request.

Wait, Xu Youyu's editor is also Qianzhou?

In Li Luo's memory, this editor, Qianzhou, was already the chief editor of the urban genre section when he first entered the industry, having little interaction with a low-tier author like himself.

He never expected that when Xu Youyu wrote novels, she was also under Qianzhou.

Before meeting Xu Youyu today, Li Luo hadn't made a particular effort to seek out people he had been connected to in his past life.

He did know that Xu Youyu wrote her first book during her high school years.

And right from her debut, it was a literary and period piece, "Literary Years." Among the various entertainment genre works at the time, it was a relatively niche and artistic type, with a very high reputation.

Even many years after it was completed, many people would still recommend this book when suggesting novels in the entertainment genre.

Previously, after Li Luo started writing "I'm Really Not a Star," he had only occasionally glanced at the top ten on the new book rankings and hadn't noticed "Literary Years" ranked further down.

At this thought, the corner of Li Luo's mouth twitched.

Honestly, he still subconsciously found it hard to connect "Literary Years" with the pretty and lively Xu Youyu in real life, because the book didn't seem like something a sixteen or seventeen-year-old girl could write.

This included the author's deep knowledge of the various experiences and gossip of the sixth-generation directors in the Beijing circle in the early 21st century, her profound understanding of the actors popular in that era, and her interpretation and delicate depiction of art-house films. It was hard to imagine that the person typing behind the keyboard was a second-year high school girl.

Especially the kinds of scenes and imagery often found in art-house films. "Sleeping Early Will Make You Taller" had described them in considerable detail in her book!

She was even smoother at writing racy scenes than he, a guy, was!

If it was just about her knowledge of that era, Xu Youyu did come from a scholarly family. Having been exposed to it from a young age, she had the means to learn and explore.

But even when it came to writing racy content, she seemed like a veteran lewd-ster who had been steeped in it for years. This senior of his, Xu, truly couldn't be judged by her appearance.

He could only say that girls did mature earlier...

Thinking this, Li Luo first accepted Xu Youyu's friend request, while simultaneously blocking her from viewing his QQ Qzone to prevent her from discovering his true identity.

Then, Li Luo replied to his editor first.

Reignition: Roger.

He then clicked open the chat window with "Sleeping Early Will Make You Taller." After some thought, he typed on the keyboard.

Reignition: Hello.

Xu Youyu was still washing dishes in the kitchen, so she naturally couldn't reply to him.

So Li Luo returned to his writing software and began tapping away, working in his bedroom.

...

Seven o'clock in the evening.

After Ying Chanxi and Xu Youyu finished the dishes and cleaned the kitchen and living room, Ying Chanxi placed the full garbage bag by the door and said to Xu Youyu, "Senior, I'll take out the trash on my way to school tomorrow morning."

"Okay, thank you for your trouble," Xu Youyu said with a smile, then added, "I'll head back to my room then. You should get to bed early too."

"Mhm." Ying Chanxi nodded and also went back to her own room, planning to study for a bit before taking a shower and going to sleep.

After Xu Youyu returned to her room, she opened QQ and, as expected, saw the message from Reignition.

Hello?

Heh, acting all cool and aloof.

The corner of Xu Youyu's mouth curled up, but she had no intention of exposing Li Luo's real identity. She sat at her desk, thought for a moment, and then typed her reply.

Sleeping Early Will Make You Taller: Hello, Big Shot!

Sleeping Early Will Make You Taller: The editor asked me to add you. Would it be convenient for us to do a chapter shout-out for each other?
